summary: Fix confirmed. With identical tensors written in two orders, eval/compare_q_llamacpp.get_storage_info at the affected commit 07ffea7f89c5 and the fix parent 9a24e0ce520a returned (21.33, 16.0, 98304) when output.weight precedes token_embd.weight, against (32.0, 16.0, 65536) when the embedding comes first: the F16 embedding fell into the layer aggregate (21.33 is exactly the bpw of embedding + F32 attn_q combined). At the fix ab875ba73053 both orders returned (32.0, 16.0, 65536).
what_ran: repro.py writes two tiny GGUF files with gguf.GGUFWriter (gguf 0.17.0): token_embd.weight and output.weight as F16 [64x32], blk.0.attn_q.weight as F32 [32x32], no norm tensors, in two orders. It calls the worktree's eval/compare_q_llamacpp.get_storage_info on each (unmodified, fresh paths so its disk cache is not reused). Environment py312-compareq-torch26cu126. The trigger needs no GPU.
limits: Synthetic GGUF files with unquantized F16/F32 tensors, not a real llama.cpp quantization. Only get_storage_info was exercised, not the VRAM figure's use in compare_q plots. Norm tensors were deliberately left out, so the fix's separate norm.weight exclusion is not tested. get_storage_info's disk_lru_cache wrote a shared __disk_lru_cache__ directory beside repro.py during the runs; it held six distinct keys (one fresh temporary path per file per commit), so no cached value crossed commits. It was removed before hashing, as a run side effect.
